model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, retention on tangible common equity

inputs.share_count_basis: ADS-EQUIVALENTS, not equity shares. Fully diluted equity shares 7,265.2m = 7,161.1m issued at 2026-03-31 (equity capital Rs 14,322m at Rs 2 face value, 20-F FY2026 balance sheet) + 104.1m dilutive employee stock options (FY26 diluted weighted 7,246.9m less basic 7,142.8m, 20-F EPS note), divided by 2 because 1 ADS = 2 equity shares (20-F cover page: 'American Depositary Shares, each representing two Equity Shares'). Held flat: ESOS/ESUS cost is expensed inside the flow, so option exercises are not also modelled as dilution. Indian banks do not buy back stock.
inputs.sbc_source: 20-F FY2026 consolidated statement of stockholders' equity, cost of employee stock options/units recognised during the year, Rs 9,687m (FY25 7,901.5m, FY24 7,029.1m; via IBN_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp). Indian ESOS/ESUS settle in new shares; there is no net-share-settlement tax line.
inputs.fcf_definition: Bank FCFE, not owner FCF. last_fcf ~= FY2026 net profit after minority interest (Rs 542,077m, after ESOS cost) less the tangible-equity retention needed to fund FY26 net-total-income growth of 8.5% at the current tangible-book/revenue ratio of 1.561 (1.561 x Rs 175,305m revenue increase = Rs 273.7bn) = ~Rs 270bn. reported_fcf adds ESOS cost back (street basis). Interest income is the bank's revenue, not an excess-cash return, so interest_income = 0.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts INR (model) to USD (quote): 1/96.30 = 0.0103842, Yahoo Finance INR=X 96.30 at 2026-10-03T03:30Z (52-week range 85.86-97.05; 20-F convenience rate at 2026-03-31 was 93.83). Per-share values are computed per ADS-equivalent (2 equity shares), so intrinsic_value is USD per IBN ADS and directly comparable to current_price. The build's *_inr twins are INR per ADS-equivalent; INR per equity share = *_inr / 2. Parity check: NSE ICICIBANK.NS close Rs 1,310.60 on 2026-10-01 (2-Oct Gandhi Jayanti holiday) x 2 / 96.30 = US$27.22 per ADS versus the IBN close at price_as_of: ADR at a ~0.8% premium to local, confirming the 1:2 ratio (1:3 would imply US$40.83).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single INR cost of equity 12.5% across all scenarios (risk charged once, via scenario weights), identical to HDB so the two India-bank ADRs are comparable. Built in the flows' own currency: India 10-year G-sec ~6.5% + beta ~0.85-0.9 x India total equity risk premium ~6.5-7.0% (mature-market ~4.3% plus India country premium) = ~12.3-12.6%; matches the 12-13% CoE range Indian brokers apply to large private banks. A USD-derived rate would understate the discount rate by the ~3pp INR/USD inflation differential.
inputs.lease_treatment: Bank: rent sits inside other operating expenses, i.e. inside profit before tax. No separate lease line; lease_cost_pct_path = 0.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, inside the flow. Minority interest (ICICI Prudential Life ~49%, ICICI Lombard ~48%, ICICI Prudential AMC ~47% outside holders) took Rs 37,285m of FY26 profit; the 'ebitda' line removes its pre-tax equivalent (37,285 / (1-0.251) = Rs 49,780m) so the flow is income to ICICI Bank common. No NCI deduction in the bridge. Listed-subsidiary stakes are valued through their consolidated earnings, not added again at market value (that would double-count).
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing table row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker'. Run as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house precedent for banks (HDB, USB, WFC, TFC, NTRS, NAB.AX); same structure as HDB so the two India-bank ADRs compare directly. Accounts are Indian GAAP consolidated (20-F primary statements, US GAAP reconciliation in notes). Engine mapping: revenue = 'Net total income' = net interest income Rs 1,061,899m + other income Rs 1,168,999m = Rs 2,230,898m (other income includes insurance premiums of the consolidated insurers; their claims/benefits sit in 'expenses pertaining to insurance business' Rs 818,364m, so the margin is net of them). 'ebitda' = profit before tax Rs 773,201m (after provisions, depreciation, insurance expenses, incl. Rs 2,629m associates) + ESOS cost 9,687 - pre-tax-equivalent minority interest 49,780 = Rs 733,108m = 32.86% of revenue. sbc_pct 0.43%. da_pct 0 (bank depreciation is an operating expense already inside PBT; branch/IT capex treated as maintenance funded within it). Tax 25.1% FY26 effective (25.3% FY25) -> 25.0% forward. 'capex' = equity retention required to grow the balance sheet = TCB/revenue (1.561) x g/(1+g): tangible book Rs 3,483bn = Rs 486.37/share (20-F: capital + ESOS outstanding + reserves, less deferred tax asset and goodwill on consolidation Rs 105.5bn) x 7,161.1m shares; DTA is deducted because RBI deducts it from CET1. Holding TCB/revenue constant keeps CET1 near today's 16.35% (regulatory minimum ~11.9% incl. CCB and 0.2% D-SIB surcharge); the ~4.5pp of CET1 headroom is NOT released to the bridge in base/bear (conservative) and is partly used in bull. FY0 check: (32.86-0.43)% x (1-0.251) x 2,230,898 = Rs 542.1bn = reported net profit after minority interest. net_debt = 0: deposits (Rs 18.3trn) and borrowings (Rs 2.2trn, incl. sub debt) are operating funding; their interest is already in the flow. FY0 ROTE ~15.6% on year-end tangible book (15.9% on average reported equity). Anchors: 20-F FY2026 (year to 2026-03-31, filed 20-Jul-2026); Q1 FY2027 6-K (Jun-26): consolidated PAT Rs 154.4bn (+13.9% YoY), NII +12.3% YoY, NIM 4.36%, GNPA 1.38%, CET1 16.19%. band_position is not meaningful: ESOS cost is 0.4% of revenue so the house/street band is a few cents wide. No buybacks; dividends Rs 78.5bn paid FY26 (payout ~16%).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: bvps_5yr_cagr (FY2021 Rs 227.9 -> FY2026 Rs 507.1 per share, reported equity / shares)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue (gross total income) CAGRs are inflated by insurance-premium consolidation (ICICI Lombard became a subsidiary Feb-2024) and the FY2023-24 rate cycle; EPS 5yr CAGR (22.7%) starts from the COVID-provisioning trough of FY2021 and is not a run-rate. Book-value growth (17-19%) exceeds what is reinvestable: payout is only ~16%, so equity compounds faster than loans and ROE has slid from 17.7% to 15.9%. The forward model uses 13-14% revenue growth, not the 17% book CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are not computed: a bank's operating cash flow and FCF are dominated by deposit/loan/investment flows and are not owner earnings. History from IBN_Metrics.csv (INR millions, consolidated Indian GAAP); FY2025-26 net total income from the 20-F FY2026 selected data table.

base.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 156.1 x g/(1+g) percent of revenue (tangible book/revenue 1.561 held constant, CET1 held near 16.35%).
base.narrative: High-teens loan growth in FY27 (management guidance; Q1 FY27 NII +12.3%) translates to ~13-14% net-total-income growth as rate cuts compress asset yields faster than deposit costs. Credit costs normalise gently from today's unusually benign level (provisions only ~2.5% of net total income), taking the pre-tax-to-common margin from 32.9% to 32.0%; ROTE ~15%. Growth fades to 7% by year 10 and 6.5% nominal INR in perpetuity (below India nominal GDP).

bull.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 148.0 x g/(1+g): CET1 allowed to drift from 16.35% toward ~15%, still ~3pp above the regulatory minimum incl. buffers.
bull.narrative: India's credit-penetration runway plus share gains from HDFC Bank's merger digestion keep loan growth at 16-17% for four years; NIM holds ~4.3% through the easing cycle as CASA reprices, fee/cross-sell income (insurance, AMC, cards) compounds, operating leverage from digital/AI underwriting lifts the margin to 34.5% (ROTE ~17-18%), and excess CET1 is deployed into growth rather than accumulated.

bear.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 156.1 x g/(1+g) percent of revenue (tangible book/revenue 1.561 held constant).
bear.narrative: The unsecured-retail cycle turns (Q1 FY27 fresh GNPA additions of Rs 27bn, card book shrinking): credit costs normalise to ~1% of loans (roughly Rs 100bn a year above today), rate cuts compress NIM toward 3.9%, and deposit competition with HDFC Bank and SBI caps growth at 8-10%. Pre-tax-to-common margin falls from 32.9% to 29%, ROTE ~13.5%, barely above the cost of equity; RBI group-structure rules force subsidiary restructuring.

scenario_narratives.base: High-teens loan growth in FY27 becomes ~13-14% net-total-income growth as rate cuts compress yields; credit costs normalise gently from an unusually benign level, taking the pre-tax-to-common margin from 32.9% to 32.0% (ROTE ~15%). Growth fades to 7% by year 10 and 6.5% nominal INR thereafter, with CET1 held near 16.35% (no excess-capital release).
scenario_narratives.bull: 16-17% loan growth for four years on India's credit runway and HDFC Bank's merger distraction, NIM held ~4.3%, fee and subsidiary income compounding and digital operating leverage lift the margin to 34.5% (ROTE ~17-18%); CET1 run down modestly toward 15%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The unsecured-retail cycle turns, credit costs rise to ~1% of loans, NIM compresses toward 3.9% under rate cuts and deposit competition; growth 8-10%, margin 29%, ROTE ~13.5%, barely above the cost of equity.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the house 15% to 20% because credit costs are at a cyclical low (provisions ~2.5% of net total income, GNPA 1.38%) and Q1 FY27 showed the first rise in fresh NPA additions; normalisation is more likely than further improvement. Bull 30% (vs house 35%) since the bull path needs both above-system growth and margin expansion during an easing cycle. Unlike HDB (25/50/25), there is no merger-integration or CEO-succession overhang: Bakhshi's term runs to Oct-2028 and asset quality is best-in-class.

entry_price.hurdle_note: 15% is applied to INR flows. With INR depreciating ~3%/yr against USD over the long run, a 15% INR IRR is roughly a 12% USD IRR for an ADR holder.

valuation_philosophy.summary: ICICI Bank is valued as a bank: free cash flow to equity (net profit to common less the tangible equity retained to fund balance-sheet growth at today's capital ratio) discounted at a 12.5% INR cost of equity, with deposits and borrowings treated as operating funding (net debt = 0). The judgment that matters is ROTE vs cost of equity vs growth: at ~15-16% ROTE and 13-14% growth, about 85% of earnings must be retained, so near-term FCFE is thin and value rests on the long growth runway and the terminal. At the current price the ADR trades at ~2.7x tangible book and ~17x FY26 EPS.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit-cost normalisation: provisions are ~Rs 56bn on a Rs 16.4trn loan book (~0.35%); a return to 1% is ~4pp of margin, the bulk of the bear case.
NIM under the RBI easing cycle (125bp of repo cuts through FY26): yields reprice faster than term deposits.
Cost of equity and terminal growth in INR: long-duration value; see the sensitivity and required-return grids.
INR/USD: values converted at spot 96.30; continued rupee depreciation lowers the USD value of an ADS independent of operations.
Excess capital: CET1 16.35% vs ~11.9% required is held, not released; a capital return or faster deployment would add value not in base.
Regulatory: RBI group-structure directions (Apr-2026) and subsidiary ownership caps; legacy former-CEO legal inquiries.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for IBN at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 25.08-33.03. Local cross-check ICICIBANK.NS (52-week range Rs 1,187.6-1,480.0) and INR=X from the same API; see inputs.fx_note.
data_sources.financials: ICICI Bank 20-F for fiscal 2026 (year to 2026-03-31): selected consolidated income statement, balance sheet, EPS note and book-value-per-share definition, read from research/IBN/Extracted/IBN_20F_FY2026.txt (INR millions, Indian GAAP consolidated). History FY2015-FY2026 and Q1 FY2027 from IBN_Metrics.csv / core_metrics.
data_sources.qualitative: IBN_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): Q1 FY2027 results, FY27 loan-growth commentary, capital, asset quality, subsidiaries.
